claim: Goyal, Jegadeesh and Wu (JFQA 2026, NYSE and Nasdaq 2012-2021): closing auctions carry about 10% of daily volume and have lower price impact than the continuous market for all stocks except Nasdaq microcaps; opening auctions are illiquid (opening auction volume is 5%-10% of closing auction volume, under 1.5% of ADV after 2015) and carry the largest price impact; long/short anomaly portfolios cost 17-41 bp per year, 9-21 bp excluding microcaps in closing auctions.
quote: Closing auctions account for about 10% of daily trading volume and offer a potentially attractive alternative to trading in the continuous market.
limitations: Costs are annualized for low-turnover anomaly portfolios, not a daily-turnover book; price impact is measured for institutional-size orders, not the effect of the auction price vs daily-bar open, which is what this step measures.
independent_replication: Working-paper version SSRN 4300417 (2022); no independent replication found.
impact_on_spec: Defines what this step does not test (opening-auction impact) and the closing-auction exit venue.

claim: UTP Plan specification (Sept 2026 edition) sale-condition table: Q = Market Center Official Open, O = Opening Prints, M = Market Center Official Close, 6 = Closing Prints; direct data recipients should use the Q value as the official market center opening value.
quote: should use the “Q” value as the official market center opening value and populate data displays accordingly.
limitations: Nasdaq (UTP) specification; the CTA equivalent for NYSE and NYSE American tapes A and B uses the same letters but is a separate document not fetched here; the check5 step verifies the codes against real trades.
impact_on_spec: Defines the condition codes used to pick official auction prices.

claim: Alpaca Market Data FAQ: the rules that decide which trades update a bar depend on tape (A, B NYSE; C Nasdaq; O OTC), the trade conditions and the bar type; a trade can have more than one condition and the strictest rule applies; the table lists per-condition whether open/close, high/low and volume are updated.
quote: A trade can have more than one condition.
limitations: The FAQ is a rendered web page; the exact per-condition table is read from the page text; there is no versioned date on the page, the published date recorded is the fetch-time year.
impact_on_spec: Explains why r_bar and r_off may differ and which condition codes to expect.

claim: Lou, Polk and Skouras (JFE 2019): for 14 trading strategies, profits are earned entirely overnight (reversal and a variety of momentum strategies) or entirely intraday, typically with profits of opposite signs across the two components.
quote: proﬁts are either earned entirely overnight (for reversal and a variety of momentum strate-
limitations: Uses first-print or official open depending on the data set and no transaction costs; not a tradability study.
independent_replication: Subsequent literature (Akbas et al. 2022, cited by Concretum) reports similar patterns.
impact_on_spec: Background for the mechanism; not a source of numeric parameters.

claim: Abdi and Ranaldo (RFS 2017): a bid-ask spread estimator from daily close, high and low prices gives the highest cross-sectional and average time-series correlations with the TAQ effective spread when quote data are unavailable, and the most accurate estimates for less liquid stocks.
quote: it generally provides the highest cross-sectional and average time-series correlations
limitations: Estimator accuracy is highest for monthly averages, noisy for single stock-days.

claim: Nagel (RFS 2012, NBER WP 17653): returns of short-term reversal strategies proxy for the returns to liquidity provision; the expected return is strongly time-varying and predictable with the VIX, rising sharply in turmoil.
quote: The returns of short-term reversal strategies in equity markets can be interpreted as a proxy for the
limitations: Monthly/weekly reversal, not intraday gap fade; paid liquidity means the edge and the cost are linked.
independent_replication: Replicated in follow-up papers on reversal and liquidity.
impact_on_spec: Mechanism background and a caveat: an edge from liquidity provision is not free of execution cost.

claim: Concretum Research (2026): stocks with abnormally large overnight gaps tend to revert the move during the following intraday session; Jan 2012 to mid-May 2026 the gross-of-cost result is CAGR about 98% and Sharpe about 2.08 with a maximum drawdown of about 67%, and the authors warn that commissions, market impact and borrow make the net picture very different.
quote: We document a distinct tendency for stocks that experience abnormally large overnight gaps to revert those moves during the subsequent intraday session
limitations: Practitioner blog, gross only, no auction-price execution study.
independent_replication: Locally reproduced in T-20260929-32 (gross short-leg Sharpe 1.33 on the easy-to-borrow proxy).

claim: Alpaca staff (2022-02-09): a Q trade is a Market Center Official Open entry that is not a real trade and can be whatever the market center defines; an O trade is an opening print, the first executed trade on a market center, and there is no standardized single authority for open prints; several market centers can report different Q or O prices for the same stock, and staff advise excluding Q from price and volume calculations for bars.
quote: It’s important to note there is no standardized single authority for open prints.
limitations: Forum post, not versioned documentation; behavior may have changed since 2022.
independent_replication: Consistent with the UTP specification footnote on Q.
impact_on_spec: Motivates the exchange-code column and the source (Q/O, M/6) tag on every fetched price.
